tasks.name: handle empty iterables in interleave_evenly
tasks.description: interleave_evenly(iterables, lengths=None) crashes with IndexError when given no iterables (interleave_evenly([]) or interleave_evenly([], lengths=[])). This happens because dims == len(lengths) == 0, and the very next block indexes lengths_desc[0] on an empty list. Every other degenerate case (one iterable, an empty sub-iterable) already returns a sensible result; this one should too: interleave_evenly([]) and interleave_evenly([], lengths=[]) should both yield nothing (an empty result), not raise.
step_by_step_implementation: After computing dims = len(lengths), check if dims == 0 (or equivalently `not dims`).
If so, return immediately (this is a generator function, so a bare `return` ends iteration and yields nothing) before any code that indexes lengths_desc/iters_desc.
Do not change any other behavior of interleave_evenly for non-empty input.

test_triad.positive: interleave_evenly([[1,2,3],[4,5]]) still yields the same Bresenham-interleaved sequence unchanged
test_triad.negative: interleave_evenly([]) currently raises IndexError; it must instead yield nothing (empty result)
test_triad.negative_to_positive: interleave_evenly([], lengths=[]) also yields nothing, and interleave_evenly([[1,2,3]]) still works normally afterward
